questionText:
Consider the following recurrence:

$$f(1) = 1;$$
$$f(2n) = 2f(n) - 1, \quad \text{for } n \ge 1;$$
$$f(2n + 1) = 2f(n) + 1, \quad \text{for } n \ge 1.$$

Then, which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
explanation:
Step-by-step evaluation of each statement:

Statement (A): $f(2^n - 1) = 2^n - 1$
• Base case for $n = 1$: $f(2^1 - 1) = f(1) = 1 = 2^1 - 1$.
• By induction, using $f(2k + 1) = 2f(k) + 1$ with $k = 2^n - 1$:
$f(2^{n+1} - 1) = f(2(2^n - 1) + 1) = 2f(2^n - 1) + 1 = 2(2^n - 1) + 1 = 2^{n+1} - 1$.
Hence, statement (A) is TRUE.

Statement (B): $f(2^n) = 1$
• Base case for $n = 1$: $f(2^1) = f(2) = 2f(1) - 1 = 2(1) - 1 = 1$.
• By induction, using $f(2k) = 2f(k) - 1$ with $k = 2^n$:
$f(2^{n+1}) = 2f(2^n) - 1 = 2(1) - 1 = 1$.
Hence, statement (B) is TRUE.

Statement (C): $f(5 \cdot 2^n) = 2^{n+1} + 1$
• Evaluating $f(5)$: since $5 = 2(2) + 1$, we get $f(5) = 2f(2) + 1 = 2(1) + 1 = 3$.
• Now applying $f(2k) = 2f(k) - 1$ repeatedly $n$ times:
$f(5 \cdot 2^n) = 2^n f(5) - (2^n - 1) = 3 \cdot 2^n - 2^n + 1 = 2 \cdot 2^n + 1 = 2^{n+1} + 1$.
Hence, statement (C) is TRUE.

Statement (D): $f(2^n + 1) = 2^n + 1$
• For $n = 2$: $f(2^2 + 1) = f(5) = 3$. However, $2^2 + 1 = 5 \neq 3$.
Hence, statement (D) is FALSE.
